name: The Shadows
description:
'''The Shadows''' (originally known as '''the Drifters''' until 1959) were an English [[instrumental rock]] group formed in 1958. Initially a [[backing band]] for [[Cliff Richard]], they began scoring hits in their own right when their single "[[Apache (instrumental)|Apache]]" reached No. 1 in the UK in 1960. They remained Richard's backing band until 1968, and joined him for several reunion tours in subsequent years. The Shadows dominated the British popular music charts in the pre-[[Beatles]] era from the late 1950s to the early 1960s, achieving 69 UK chart singles from the 1950s to the 2000s, 35 as the Shadows and 34 as '''Cliff Richard and the Shadows''', ranging from [[Pop music|pop]], [[Rock music|rock]], [[surf rock]] and [[Sentimental ballad|ballads]] with a [[jazz]] influence. The group, who were in the forefront of the UK [[beat-group]] boom, were the first backing band to also achieve commercial success in their own right.

The group's first settled line-up consisted of lead guitarist [[Hank Marvin]], rhythm guitarist [[Bruce Welch]], bass guitarist  [[Jet Harris]] and drummer [[Tony Meehan]]. Marvin remained with the group for its whole history. Welch departed in 1968 but rejoined in 1973. [[Brian Bennett]] replaced Meehan in 1961 and remained the Shadows' drummer from then on. Harris left in 1962, from which time the group had various bass guitarists.

As pioneers of the four-member instrumental format (lead guitar, rhythm guitar, bass guitar and drums), the Shadows built their signature sound on [[Fender Musical Instruments Corporation|Fender]] guitars and [[Vox (musical equipment)|Vox]] amplifiers, but around 1964, they replaced their Fenders with [[Burns London|Burns]] guitars, with Bruce Welch citing tuning issues as the main reason.
